drivers.name: Christie Projector
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Christie commercial projectors using the Christie Serial API on TCP 3002. Supports the M, J, HS, H, GS, G, and E series families and their derivatives. Power, shutter, fade-to-black, input select, test patterns, brightness/contrast, freeze, orientation, lamp mode, lamp intensity, and lens focus. Polls for status; the projector also reports model, firmware, and projector hours.

help.overview: Christie commercial projectors that speak the Christie Serial API (M Series, J Series, HS / H Series, GS / G Series, E Series, Roadie). Power, shutter, fade-to-black, input select, brightness, contrast, freeze, orientation, test patterns, lamp mode, lamp intensity, and lens focus. Polls every 30 seconds for status. For commands not exposed here, use Send Raw Command — the full command list is in the Christie Serial API Technical Reference for your projector series.
help.setup:
1. Connect the projector to your network. 2. On the projector menu, enable Ethernet and note the IP address. 3. The Christie Serial API listens on TCP 3002 by default and does
   not require authentication.
4. Set the projector's "Serial Mode" / "Serial API" to enabled if
   it is not already on. (M Series MENU > Configuration >
   Communications > Network Settings.)
5. The Input Select command takes a two-digit slot+input code
   (e.g. 12 = slot 1 input 2). The slot/input map is on the back
   panel of the projector.

compatible_models.notes: All series share the same (CODE) message format and the core power / shutter / input / image controls. Series-specific features (e.g. laser-light controls on HS, lens-shift codes on GS) are not exposed here; use send_command with the series' published command list when needed. Boxer / Inspire / 4KHS / Crimson use a newer JSON / Christie API and require a different driver — they are not covered here.

drivers.name: PJLink Class 1 Projector
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls any PJLink Class 1 compatible projector.

help.overview: Universal projector control via the PJLink Class 1 standard. Works with 100+ models from Epson, NEC, Panasonic, Sony, Christie, Hitachi, BenQ, Optoma, Canon, and Vivitek.
help.setup:
1. Enable network control on the projector (varies by manufacturer)
2. Assign a static IP address to the projector
3. If authentication is enabled, set the PJLink password
4. Default port is 4352 (PJLink standard)

drivers.name: Sharp NEC Projector
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Sharp NEC projectors via the NEC binary control protocol over TCP. Compatible with P, PA, PE, PV, PX, ME, and M series projectors.

help.overview: Full-featured Sharp NEC projector control using the proprietary binary protocol on TCP port 7142. Power, input selection, picture/sound/OSD mute, freeze, shutter, volume, brightness, contrast, sharpness, aspect ratio, eco mode, lens control (zoom/focus/shift), lens memory presets, lamp/laser hours, filter hours, and detailed error status.
help.setup:
1. Connect the projector to the network
2. Enable LAN control in the projector's network settings
3. Assign a static IP address to the projector
4. Default control port is 7142
5. This driver can coexist with PJLink (port 4352)
6. Set Standby Mode to 'Network Standby' or 'Sleep' to allow power-on via network
7. Input terminal codes vary by model — unsupported inputs are rejected gracefully

compatible_models.notes: Per NEC protocol manual. Specific models like NP-P506QL fall under P series.
